claim: Sedimentation velocity analytical ultracentrifugation equipped with fluorescence detection (FDS-SV) allows the characterization of protein complexes free in solution with high size resolution, at concentrations in the nanomolar and picomolar range.
source: Sedimentation velocity analytical ultracentrifugation equipped with fluorescence detection (FDS-SV) allows the characterization of protein complexes free in solution with high size resolution, at concentrations in the nanomolar and picomolar range.
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to prior work and is consistent with established knowledge about FDS-SV capabilities.

claim: The MCMC approach facilitates studies of heterogeneous multi-protein complexes at orders of magnitude lower concentrations and for higher-affinity systems than previously possible.
source: This novel approach facilitates studies of heterogeneous multi-protein complexes at orders of magnitude lower concentrations and for higher-affinity systems than previously possible.
evidence: This is a primary claim about the capabilities of the new method, supported by the experimental results presented in the manuscript.

claim: The dynamic formation of multi-protein complexes is a key step in the assembly of supramolecular structures and in the regulation of many cellular processes.
source: The dynamic formation of multi-protein complexes is a key step in the assembly of supramolecular structures and in the regulation of many cellular processes (Wu, 2013; Li et al., 2012; Gavin et al., 2002; Krogan et al., 2006; Wu and Fuxreiter, 2016).
evidence: This statement is supported by multiple citations to prior literature.

claim: In immunological signal transduction the assembly of adaptor protein complexes into micro-clusters after T-cell activation plays a critical role in the sensitivity and specificity of activation.
source: For example, in immunological signal transduction the assembly of adaptor protein complexes into micro-clusters after T-cell activation plays a critical role in the sensitivity and specificity of activation (Sherman et al., 2011; Dustin and Groves, 2012).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to prior research.

claim: The post-synaptic density is a large structure assembled via interactions between many different scaffolding proteins, signaling proteins and ligand gated ion channels, that regulates postsynaptic neurotransmission and plasticity.
source: Another well-known multi-protein complex is the post-synaptic density, a large structure assembled via interactions between many different scaffolding proteins, signaling proteins and ligand gated ion channels, that regulates postsynaptic neurotransmission and plasticity (Kennedy, 2000; Ferré et al., 2007; Kumar and Mayer, 2012).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to prior literature.

claim: Many of the protein interactions involved in the assembly of molecular machinery are multivalent.
source: Many of the protein interactions involved in the assembly of such molecular machinery are multivalent (Li et al., 2012; Houtman et al., 2006; Coussens et al., 2013).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to prior research.

claim: Multivalent interactions often allow structurally polymorph complexes to co-exist.
source: This often allows structurally polymorph complexes to co-exist (Wu and Fuxreiter, 2016), posing formidable challenges for any biophysical method to elucidate basic architectural principles and driving forces, which requires the study of reversible interactions of multiple protein components with multiple states.
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to prior work.

claim: Sedimentation velocity analytical ultracentrifugation (SV) allows determination of the number, size, and shape of reversibly formed protein complexes, and provides information on their affinity, stoichiometry and binding kinetics.
source: Sedimentation velocity analytical ultracentrifugation (SV) is a classical technique that allows determination of the number, size, and shape of reversibly formed protein complexes, and provides information on their affinity, stoichiometry and binding kinetics (Schuck, 2013, 2015).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to prior work describing SV capabilities.

claim: In SV, faster sedimenting protein complexes will always remain in a bath of slower-sedimenting constituent components, such that the association/dissociation of non-covalent complexes is maintained throughout the experiment.
source: SV has unique opportunities for studying protein interactions, since—different from separation techniques—faster sedimenting protein complexes will always remain in a bath of slower-sedimenting constituent components, such that the association/dissociation of non-covalent complexes is maintained throughout the experiment (Figure 1).
evidence: This statement is supported by reference to Figure 1 which illustrates the principle, and is based on established knowledge of SV.

claim: SV has emerged as a powerful technique in the study of the solution state behavior of complex interacting systems of macromolecules, including ion-channels, adaptor proteins, membrane proteins, nucleic acids, and carbohydrates.
source: Thus, SV has emerged as a powerful technique in the study of the solution state behavior of complex interacting systems of macromolecules, including ion-channels, adaptor proteins, membrane proteins, nucleic acids, and carbohydrates (Kumar and Mayer, 2012; Houtman et al., 2005; le Maire et al., 2008 Niewiarowski et al., 2010; Padrick and Brautigam, 2011; Harding et al., 2015; Jose et al., 2012).
evidence: This statement is supported by multiple citations to prior applications of SV.

claim: Extended to multi-signal analysis SV can distinguish different sedimenting components from characteristic extinction properties, directly revealing binding stoichiometries and resolving co-existing complexes.
source: Extended to multi-signal analysis SV can distinguish different sedimenting components from characteristic extinction properties, directly revealing binding stoichiometries and resolving co-existing complexes (Houtman et al., 2006; Coussens et al., 2013; Padrick and Brautigam, 2011; Balbo et al., 2005; Barda-Saad et al., 2010).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to prior work on multi-signal SV analysis.

claim: An essential mechanism for the formation of signaling particles in T-cell activation was discovered to be the multivalent intracellular oligomerization of LAT via three-component adaptor protein complexes.
source: For example, through applications of this approach an essential mechanism for the formation of signaling particles in T-cell activation (Houtman et al., 2006; Coussens et al., 2013; Barda-Saad et al., 2010) was discovered to be the multivalent intracellular oligomerization of LAT via three-component adaptor protein complexes (Houtman et al., 2006).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to prior research.

claim: Traditional SV is limited by optical detection systems that generally require the use of micromolar concentrations of purified proteins.
source: But, unfortunately, traditional SV is limited in several ways by optical detection systems that generally require the use of micromolar concentrations of purified proteins.
evidence: This statement is based on established knowledge about the limitations of traditional SV detection systems.

claim: Analytical ultracentrifugation was enhanced by the availability of a commercial fluorescence optical detection system (FDS), that uses confocal detection radially scanning the sample in the spinning rotor.
source: Recently, analytical ultracentrifugation was enhanced by the availability of a commercial fluorescence optical detection system (FDS), that uses confocal detection radially scanning the sample in the spinning rotor (MacGregor et al., 2004) (Figure 2a).
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to prior work and reference to Figure 2a.

claim: The FDS allows highly quantitative analyses of the sedimentation process.
source: After accounting for characteristic data features, the FDS allows highly quantitative analyses of the sedimentation process (Zhao et al., 2013b), extending the sensitivity of SV by several orders of magnitude into the low picomolar range (Zhao et al., 2014a; Le Roy et al., 2015).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to prior work.

claim: FDS extends the sensitivity of SV by several orders of magnitude into the low picomolar range.
source: After accounting for characteristic data features, the FDS allows highly quantitative analyses of the sedimentation process (Zhao et al., 2013b), extending the sensitivity of SV by several orders of magnitude into the low picomolar range (Zhao et al., 2014a; Le Roy et al., 2015).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to prior work.

claim: FDS enables the measurement of binding energies in self- and hetero-association with very high affinity.
source: This enables the measurement of binding energies in self- and hetero-association with very high affinity (Zhao et al., 2012; 2013a; 2014a), and also makes it possible to study proteins that are relatively scarce, not well purified, and in some cases even in cell extracts (Le Roy et al., 2015; Polling et al., 2013; Kingsbury and Laue, 2011; Kokona et al., 2015).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to prior work.

claim: FDS makes it possible to study proteins that are relatively scarce, not well purified, and in some cases even in cell extracts.
source: This enables the measurement of binding energies in self- and hetero-association with very high affinity (Zhao et al., 2012; 2013a; 2014a), and also makes it possible to study proteins that are relatively scarce, not well purified, and in some cases even in cell extracts (Le Roy et al., 2015; Polling et al., 2013; Kingsbury and Laue, 2011; Kokona et al., 2015).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to prior work.

claim: FDS has only a single excitation wavelength, either 488 nm or 561 nm, due to the technical constraints of accommodating a moveable confocal optical system inside the evacuated rotor chamber of the ultracentrifuge.
source: Unfortunately, these advantages come with a drawback of having only a single excitation wavelength, either 488 nm or 561 nm, due to the technical constraints of accommodating a moveable confocal optical system inside the evacuated rotor chamber of the ultracentrifuge.
evidence: This statement describes a technical limitation of the FDS system based on its design constraints.

claim: Spectral discrimination of multiple components is not available in AUC fluorescence detection, which significantly limits the study of multi-protein complexes.
source: Thus, spectral discrimination of multiple components is not available in AUC fluorescence detection, which significantly limits the study of multi-protein complexes.
evidence: This statement is an inference from the single-wavelength limitation of FDS.

claim: Photoswitchable fluorescent proteins (psFPs) can be actively switched between fluorescent and non-fluorescent states using different wavelengths of illumination.
source: In the present work, we embark on a different approach for multi-component analysis based on photophysical properties of photoswitchable fluorescent proteins (psFPs). The psFPs make up a class of fluorescent proteins that can be actively switched between fluorescent and non-fluorescent states using different wavelengths of illumination.
evidence: This statement is based on established knowledge about psFPs.

claim: Under the illumination conditions of FDS-SV, psFPs are induced to slowly switch by virtue of the excitation light when radially scanning the spinning sample.
source: While they have been engineered for entirely different purposes in nanoscience and fluorescence imaging, we have previously observed that under the illumination conditions of FDS-SV they are induced to slowly switch by virtue of the excitation light when radially scanning the spinning sample (Zhao et al., 2014b).
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to prior work.

claim: In the low-power exposure that occurs during sedimentation using the FDS, the photoswitching process is quantitatively modeled very well as a single exponential.
source: Even though the mechanism of photoswitching in psFPs generally may involve multiple states, in the low-power exposure that occurs during sedimentation using the FDS the process is quantitatively modeled very well as a single exponential.
evidence: This statement is supported by the experimental data and modeling presented in the manuscript.

claim: Different classes of psFPs exhibit different time-courses of photoswitching in FDS-SV.
source: Different classes of psFPs exhibit different time-courses of photoswitching in FDS-SV, and may be switched on to a fluorescent state or switched off to a dark state.
evidence: This statement is supported by the experimental data shown in Figure 2.

claim: The spatio-temporal signal modulation from photoswitching can be folded into the computational analysis of the sedimentation process to offer an avenue for monochromatic multi-component (MCMC) detection.
source: The new spatio-temporal signal dimension is folded into the computational analysis of the sedimentation process, and thus offers an avenue for monochromatic multi-component (MCMC) detection.
evidence: This is a primary claim about the method developed in this work, supported by the experimental results.

claim: The MCMC approach allows simultaneous determination of separate sedimentation coefficient distributions for each class of fluorophore.
source: Using existing commercial FDS instrumentation, the MCMC approach allows us to simultaneously determine separate sedimentation coefficient distributions for each class of fluorophore, which can be used to determine the identity and binding stoichiometry of hydrodynamically resolved complexes of psFP-tagged proteins.
evidence: This statement is supported by the experimental results presented in the manuscript.

claim: The MCMC approach can be used to determine the identity and binding stoichiometry of hydrodynamically resolved complexes of psFP-tagged proteins.
source: Using existing commercial FDS instrumentation, the MCMC approach allows us to simultaneously determine separate sedimentation coefficient distributions for each class of fluorophore, which can be used to determine the identity and binding stoichiometry of hydrodynamically resolved complexes of psFP-tagged proteins.
evidence: This statement is supported by the experimental results presented in the manuscript.

claim: Glutamate receptor GluA2 and GluA3 amino terminal domains engage in competitive homo-dimerization and hetero-dimerization processes.
source: We then use this approach to study the high-affinity interactions of glutamate receptor GluA2 and GluA3 amino terminal domains, which engage in competitive homo-dimerization and hetero-dimerization processes that are thought to control the combination of receptor subtypes into diverse homomeric and heteromeric ion channel tetramers with different gating properties (Kumar and Mayer, 2012; Rossmann et al., 2011; Herguedas et al., 2016).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to prior work.

claim: The dimerization of GluA2 and GluA3 amino terminal domains is thought to control the combination of receptor subtypes into diverse homomeric and heteromeric ion channel tetramers with different gating properties.
source: We then use this approach to study the high-affinity interactions of glutamate receptor GluA2 and GluA3 amino terminal domains, which engage in competitive homo-dimerization and hetero-dimerization processes that are thought to control the combination of receptor subtypes into diverse homomeric and heteromeric ion channel tetramers with different gating properties (Kumar and Mayer, 2012; Rossmann et al., 2011; Herguedas et al., 2016).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to prior work.

claim: Fluorescence SV signals of psFPs exhibit sedimentation boundaries modulated by characteristic signal magnification or diminution on the time-scale of sedimentation.
source: Fluorescence SV signals of psFPs are highly unusual when compared to the temporal evolution of concentration profiles in traditional AUC (Figure 2b), in that they exhibit sedimentation boundaries modulated by characteristic signal magnification or diminution on the time-scale of sedimentation (Figure 2c,d).
evidence: This statement is supported by the data shown in Figures 2c and 2d.

claim: The signal modulation in psFPs is caused by the 488 nm excitation beam of the FDS scanner which induces photoswitching between fluorescent and dark states.
source: This is caused by the 488 nm excitation beam of the FDS scanner which induces photoswitching between fluorescent and dark states.
evidence: This statement is an inference from the observed signal behavior and the known properties of psFPs.

claim: The transient exposure in FDS-SV during radial scanning and sample rotation leads to a time-averaged incident power density that is ~10^5-fold weaker than typical power densities for photoswitching on the millisecond time-scale.
source: But in contrast to typical power densities of ~ kW/cm2 for photoswitching on the millisecond time-scale (Grotjohann et al., 2012), the transient exposure in FDS-SV during radial scanning and sample rotation leads to a time-averaged incident power density that is ~105-fold weaker.
evidence: This statement is based on calculations comparing FDS-SV exposure to typical photoswitching conditions, with citation to prior work.

claim: The weaker power density in FDS-SV slows the photoswitching kinetics down to the time-scale of hours, commensurate with the sedimentation process in SV.
source: This slows the photoswitching kinetics down to the time-scale of hours, commensurate with the sedimentation process in SV.
evidence: This statement is an inference from the observed photoswitching behavior in FDS-SV.

claim: A model assuming a single-step process with constant quantum efficiency for switching, while accounting for the radially non-uniform exposure during scanning, can precisely describe the signal evolution of individual psFPs.
source: We have developed a model Equation 4 that assumes a single-step process with constant quantum efficiency for switching, while accounting for the radially non-uniform exposure during scanning (caused by psFPs transitioning through the beam in a shorter time as they migrate to higher radii at the same angular velocity).
evidence: This statement is supported by the model development and the quality of fits to experimental data shown in Figure 2.

claim: The model predicts signal boundaries to be subject to an exponential overall signal modulation with slightly radially sloping solution plateaus.
source: Combined with a description of molecular sedimentation and diffusion, the model predicts signal boundaries to be subject to an exponential overall signal modulation with slightly radially sloping solution plateaus, with a small positive slope for those switching off (Figure 2c) and a small negative slope for FPs switching on (Figure 2d) under 488 nm illumination.
evidence: This statement is supported by the model predictions and the data shown in Figures 2c and 2d.

claim: For rsEGFP with a scanning beam of 13 mW, the depletion rate is 5.08 [4.97–5.19; 95% CI]×10^-4/sec, approaching a final fluorescence of 13.4 [13.0–13.9; 95% CI]% its initial value.
source: For example, for rsEGFP with a scanning beam of 13 mW we measure a depletion rate of 5.08 [4.97–5.19; 95% CI]×10–4/sec, approaching a final fluorescence of 13.4 [13.0–13.9; 95% CI]% its initial value, associated with a particle sedimentation coefficient of 2.50 [2.45–2.54; 95% CI] S and apparent molar mass of 29.5 [26.5–33.0; 95% CI] kDa.
evidence: This statement reports experimental measurements with confidence intervals.

claim: rsEGFP has a particle sedimentation coefficient of 2.50 [2.45–2.54; 95% CI] S and apparent molar mass of 29.5 [26.5–33.0; 95% CI] kDa.
source: For example, for rsEGFP with a scanning beam of 13 mW we measure a depletion rate of 5.08 [4.97–5.19; 95% CI]×10–4/sec, approaching a final fluorescence of 13.4 [13.0–13.9; 95% CI]% its initial value, associated with a particle sedimentation coefficient of 2.50 [2.45–2.54; 95% CI] S and apparent molar mass of 29.5 [26.5–33.0; 95% CI] kDa.
evidence: This statement reports experimental measurements with confidence intervals.

claim: No photophysical processes are detectable under 13 mW illumination for fluorophores such as fluorescein-based DL488 and standard EGFP.
source: By contrast, as previously established (Zhao et al., 2014b), no photophysical processes are detectable under this illumination for other fluorophores such as fluorescein-based DL488 (Figure 2b) and standard EGFP.
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to prior work and reference to Figure 2b.

claim: The strikingly different signal patterns in sedimentation of psFPs can be utilized for the computational decomposition of sedimentation data of mixtures into separate sedimentation coefficient distributions for each differently tagged component.
source: The strikingly different signal patterns in sedimentation of psFPs can be utilized for the computational decomposition of sedimentation data of mixtures into separate sedimentation coefficient distributions for each differently tagged component.
evidence: This statement is supported by the experimental results shown in Figure 3.

claim: In a mixture of rsEGFP2 and FITC-BSA, the initially strongly decreasing plateau intensity over time is a characteristic of rsEGFP2 signals that can be readily visually discerned and distinguished from the stable fluorescein signal.
source: The shape of the signal boundaries is governed jointly by the signal time-domain, polydispersity in the sedimentation coefficient distribution, as well as diffusion. The initially strongly decreasing plateau intensity over time is a characteristics of rsEGFP2 signals that can be readily visually discerned and distinguished from the stable fluorescein signal that causes the plateaus to stabilize at approximately half the total loading signal.
evidence: This statement is supported by the data shown in Figure 3a.

claim: The MCMC decomposition of a mixture of rsEGFP2 and FITC-BSA results in sedimentation coefficient distributions highly consistent with those obtained in control experiments of individual protein components.
source: The sedimentation coefficients extracted from the mixture are highly consistent with those obtained in control experiments of individual protein components (dashed lines in Figure 3c), as expected for a mixture of non-interacting species.
evidence: This statement is supported by the comparison shown in Figure 3c.

claim: The relative errors in the distinction between rsEGFP2 and fluorescein components in the mixture are calculated to be 0.21% over the entire range.
source: The relative errors in the distinction between rsEGFP2 and fluorescein components are calculated to be 0.21% over the entire range (based on Equation 6).
evidence: This statement reports a calculated error estimate based on the model.

claim: In a three-protein mixture of rsEGFP2, Padron, and anti-GFP mAb, the sedimentation coefficient distribution of rsEGFP2 shows a 7 S peak with no 2.5 S peak, consistent with the formation of an antibody/rsEGFP2 complex.
source: Here, the sedimentation coefficient distribution of rsEGFP2 shows a 7 S peak with no 2.5 S peak, consistent with the formation of an antibody/rsEGFP2 complex.
evidence: This statement is supported by the data shown in Figure 3f.

claim: The binding partner of the antibody can be correctly identified by exploiting the temporal signature dimension characteristic of the psFPs.
source: Thus, the binding partner of the antibody can be correctly identified by exploiting the new temporal signature dimension characteristic of the psFPs.
evidence: This statement is supported by the experimental results shown in Figure 3.

claim: The relative error in assignment of component concentrations in the three-protein mixture is 2.6% at 2.5 S and 1.1% at 7 S.
source: Based on Equation 6, the relative error in assignment of component concentrations is 2.6% at 2.5 S and 1.1% at 7 S.
evidence: This statement reports calculated error estimates based on the model.

claim: When bound by the anti-GFP antibody, rsEGFP2 shows a portion of the fast-moving boundary remaining fluorescent after long time (α = 0.2070 [0.2052–0.2088, 95% CI]), whereas free rsEGFP2 shows nearly complete conversion to the dark state (α = 0.0274 [0.0270–0.0281, 95% CI]).
source: As may already be visually discerned from comparison with Figure 3—figure supplement 1, a portion of the fast-moving boundary of the rsEGFP2/mAb complex in Figure 3d remains fluorescent after long time (α = 0.2070 [0.2052–0.2088, 95% CI]), whereas free rsEGFP2 shows nearly complete conversion to the dark state (α = 0.0274 [0.0270–0.0281, 95% CI]).
evidence: This statement reports experimental measurements with confidence intervals, supported by comparison of figures.

claim: When bound by the anti-GFP antibody, the contrast of rsEGFP2 is lower than in the unbound state.
source: Clearly, when bound by the anti-GFP antibody, the contrast of rsEGFP2 is lower than in the unbound state.
evidence: This statement is an inference from the experimental measurements.

claim: rsEGFP exhibits slightly altered photoswitching kinetics in the presence of the anti-GFP antibody.
source: Similar observations were made with rsEGFP, which exhibits slightly altered photoswitching kinetics in the presence of the anti-GFP antibody (data not shown).
evidence: This statement reports an observation from data not shown.

claim: Benchtop fluorimeter measurements confirmed marked alterations in the off rates and on/off contrast ratios for both rsEGFP and rsEGFP2 in the presence of antibody as compared to their unbound state.
source: These observations were confirmed by rsEGFP and rsEGFP2 fluorescence measurements in a benchtop fluorimeter (Figure 4a), where we found marked alterations in the off rates and on/off contrast ratios for both rsEGFP and rsEGFP2 in the presence of antibody as compared to their unbound state.
evidence: This statement is supported by the data shown in Figure 4a.

claim: The emission spectral properties of rsEGFP and rsEGFP2 changed little with the addition of the antibody.
source: At the same time, their emission spectral properties changed little with the addition of the antibody (Figure 4b).
evidence: This statement is supported by the data shown in Figure 4b.

claim: The effects of antibody binding on photoswitching point to possible conformational changes induced by antibody binding impacting the equilibrium of photophysical states.
source: These effects point to possible conformational changes induced by antibody binding impacting the equilibrium of photophysical states (see Discussion).
evidence: This statement is a speculative interpretation of the experimental observations.

claim: Several psFPs are suitable for FDS-SV with well-defined photophysical characteristics under the current illumination conditions, including rsEGFP, rsEGFP2, Padron, and Dronpa.
source: We have found that several psFPs are suitable for FDS-SV with well-defined photophysical characteristics under the current illumination conditions. Besides rsEGFP, rsEGFP2 and Padron these also include Dronpa (Zhao et al., 2014b).
evidence: This statement is supported by experimental observations and a citation to prior work.

claim: Newer FDS models operate with an adjustable 50 mW diode laser that offers additional flexibility for modulating photoswitching kinetics by using different power settings for the scanning beam.
source: While older FDS instruments are equipped with a fixed-power 13 mW solid-state laser, newer models operate with an adjustable 50 mW diode laser that offers additional flexibility for modulating photoswitching kinetics by using different power settings for the scanning beam.
evidence: This statement describes technical specifications of FDS instruments.

claim: The optimal choice of psFP and excitation power will be determined by consideration of the temporal conversion characteristics of all psFPs in the mixture, in combination with the expected time-course of sedimentation.
source: The optimal choice of psFP and excitation power will be determined by consideration of the temporal conversion characteristics of all psFPs in the mixture, in combination with the expected time-course of sedimentation, as dictated by s-value of the protein complex and the rotor speed.
evidence: This statement is a recommendation based on the theoretical analysis.

claim: Equation 6 has been implemented in the data analysis software as a design tool that can guide the psFP selection to maximize the contrast for MCMC based on known psFP characteristics in FDS and the sedimentation coefficient range of the expected protein complexes.
source: We have implemented Equation 6 in the data analysis software as a design tool that – prior to data acquisition – can guide the psFP selection to maximize the contrast for MCMC based on known psFP characteristics in FDS and the sedimentation coefficient range of the expected protein complexes.
evidence: This statement describes a computational tool developed as part of this work.

claim: For a 2.8 S species under standard SV conditions, the theoretically best switching rate constant is between 1–5×10^-4/sec.
source: For example, the black line in Figure 5 shows the theoretically best switching rate constant for a 2.8 S species under standard SV conditions to be between 1–5×10–4/sec.
evidence: This statement is supported by the theoretical calculations shown in Figure 5.

claim: Switching of psFPs is required for discrimination, but decaying boundary amplitudes for psFPs that switch off during sedimentation will diminish the information content on such psFPs-tagged species, as the signal disappears at later times.
source: It is evident that switching of psFPs is required for discrimination, but at the same time the decaying boundary amplitudes for psFPs that switch off during sedimentation will diminish the information content on such psFPs-tagged species, as the signal disappears at later times.
evidence: This statement is an inference from the observed signal behavior.

claim: Rapid and virtually complete restoration of the initial psFPs signal is possible by illumination at 405 nm.
source: However, rapid and virtually complete restoration of the initial psFPs signal is possible by illumination at 405 nm.
evidence: This statement is based on known properties of psFPs and experimental observations.

claim: rsEGFP and rsEGFP2 can undergo hundreds of on/off cycles with very little loss.
source: In this way, for example, rsEGFP and rsEGFP2 can undergo hundreds of on/off cycles with very little loss (Grotjohann et al., 2012).
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to prior work.

claim: A modified Optima XL-A was used where 405 nm light from a high-power LED was guided into the rotor chamber through the interference optics port to illuminate the spinning rotor.
source: To this end, we took advantage of the window in the rotor chamber that usually forms part of the interference optical system, and modified it to allow illumination of the spinning rotor with a high-power 405 nm LED at ~10 mW/cm2.
evidence: This statement describes an instrument modification made for this work.

claim: A sector-shaped mask was used to produce constant 405 nm exposure times for molecules rotating through the beam at all radii.
source: To achieve a quantitatively uniform reset of fluorescence, a sector-shaped mask was used to produce constant 405 nm exposure times for molecules rotating through the beam at all radii.
evidence: This statement describes an experimental design element.

claim: SV experiments with several cycles of rapid signal depletion under 488 nm illumination at 25 mW (producing a depletion rate of 9.7×10^-4/s for rsEGFP2), alternating with a 2 min pulse of 405 nm illumination (leading to > 98% recovery of the fluorescence signal of rsEGFP2) were carried out.
source: SV experiments were carried out with several cycles of rapid signal depletion under 488 nm illumination at 25 mW (producing a depletion rate of 9.7×10–4/s for rsEGFP2), alternating with a 2 min pulse of 405 nm illumination (leading to > 98% recovery of the fluorescence signal of rsEGFP2).
evidence: This statement describes experimental conditions and reports measurements.

claim: Blinking SV data could be fitted within the noise of data acquisition, and blinking has been fully implemented in the MCMC decomposition of signals from mixtures with different fluorophores.
source: An experiment with Padron exhibiting the opposite blinking behavior is shown in Figure 6b. With signal recovery time-points included into the model, blinking SV data could be fitted within the noise of data acquisition, and blinking has been fully implemented in the MCMC decomposition of signals from mixtures with different fluorophores.
evidence: This statement is supported by the data shown in Figure 6b and the model development.

claim: For switching processes at rates below 3×10^-4/sec, blinking can be detrimental to component discrimination, because it does not allow the fluorophore to ever significantly populate the dark state.
source: However, on the basis of the theoretical analysis of information content in Figure 5 (magenta line), for switching processes at rates below 3×10–4/sec, blinking can be detrimental to component discrimination, because it does not allow the fluorophore to ever significantly populate the dark state.
evidence: This statement is based on the theoretical analysis shown in Figure 5.

claim: A spatially localized trough in the psFP fluorescence signal can be created by positioning the existing FDS detector at a fixed radius for an extended period of time at the beginning of the sedimentation process.
source: For the slow switching case, we followed a different approach to enhance discrimination by creating a spatially localized trough in the psFP fluorescence signal. In contrast to blinking, this can be executed without any instrument modification, simply by positioning the existing FDS detector at a fixed radius for an extended period of time at the beginning of the sedimentation process.
evidence: This statement describes an experimental approach developed in this work.

claim: The stationary exposure is estimated to be on the order of 100-fold stronger as compared to the time-averaged exposure during scanning across the standard radial scan range.
source: Based on the size of the focal spot we estimate the stationary exposure to be on the order of 100-fold stronger as compared to the time-averaged exposure during scanning across the standard radial scan range.
evidence: This statement is an estimate based on calculations.

claim: The FRAP-like SV model requires the additional application of appropriate boundary conditions at early times to account for the initial localized switching.
source: Even though this appears to be a more complicated process, the evolution of the trough is naturally modeled in the same framework developed above for the sedimentation in quasi-uniform exposure: Since SV models already account for diffusional spread superimposed to sedimentation, the FRAP-like SV model solely requires the additional application of appropriate boundary conditions (Equation 8) at early times.
evidence: This statement describes the modeling approach for FRAP-like SV.

claim: FRAP-like SV data are enriched in several ways: (1) additional information on diffusion becomes available; (2) two additional sedimentation boundaries are generated to improve the precision of sedimentation coefficients; and (3) in data from mixtures of psFPs with stable fluorescent molecules, the depth of the trough will provide a landmark at early times reporting directly on the concentration of psFPs-tagged components.
source: However, in comparison to standard sedimentation boundaries, the resulting data are enriched in several ways, as (1) additional information on diffusion becomes available; (2) two additional sedimentation boundaries are generated to improve the precision of sedimentation coefficients; and (3) in data from mixtures of psFPs with stable fluorescent molecules, the depth of the trough will provide a landmark at early times reporting directly on the concentration of psFPs-tagged components.
evidence: This statement describes advantages of the FRAP-like SV approach based on theoretical considerations.

claim: Excellent fits were achieved with the FRAP-like SV model with residuals close to the noise of data acquisition.
source: In applications to the analysis of experimental data, excellent fits were achieved with this model with residuals close to the noise of data acquisition.
evidence: This statement is supported by the experimental results shown in Figure 2f.

claim: For rsEGFP2-GluA3 data with initial localized switching, the s-value is 4.59 [4.50–4.68, 68% CI] S, consistent with the value obtained from blinking and from constant illumination experiments.
source: For example, with the single-species model fitted to the rsEGFP2-GluA3 data shown in Figure 2f, the s-value is 4.59 [4.50–4.68, 68% CI] S, consistent with the value obtained from blinking and from constant illumination experiments.
evidence: This statement reports experimental measurements with confidence intervals.

claim: Glutamate receptor ion channels (iGluRs) assemble into homo- and hetero-tetramers with their subtype composition dictating the properties of synaptic transmission.
source: Glutamate receptor ion channels (iGluRs) assemble into homo- and hetero-tetramers with their subtype composition dictating the properties of synaptic transmission (Geiger et al., 1995).
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to prior work.
